ownerNotes: PK1-8 (review round 1) and the lane monitor: a receipt whose status or counts disagree with rules kept out of this contract is refused by R12. A probe kit built from this draft alone can show the interface form, but not acceptance, because the withheld status and count rules stay with R12. kitNotes: PK3-1 (review round 3), carried by the lane monitor's Q-PK6-PK3-1 (a) as complete form text for the kit author; it adds to G14 and /http/transport/serverCertificate, and the client refuses a server certificate that misses any of it. The server certificate carries the basic-constraints, extended-key-usage and subjectAltName extensions; it is a leaf, not a CA; its extended key usage is exactly server authentication; it has at most 32 subjectAltNames, each a DNS name, a URI or an IP address; and, as G14 states, the endpoint's tls.serverName is among its DNS subjectAltNames, no subjectAltName holds a wildcard, its public key is the pinned one, and its chain verifies against the configured CA. No certificate, key, name or digest value is part of this contract, and no validity-window rule is stated here.
nonClaims: This draft records the interface form only; it does not state or imply that any probe output will be accepted by R12.
